name: Bird of Paradise
description:
Michalina Janoszanka (1889–1952)

A bright-feathered bird grips a golden branch among dark-hearted blossoms, set against deep black.

Janoszanka, a Polish painter from Kraków, is best known for pictures like this one, painted in reverse on the back of a sheet of glass.

name: Butterfly
description:
Michalina Janoszanka (1889–1952)

A patterned butterfly drifts past a gilded tree at the water's edge, under a night-black sky threaded with fine white lines.

Painted in reverse on glass.

name: Spring
description:
Michalina Janoszanka (1889–1952)

A speckled frog sits among toadstools beside a dark pond of water lilies, beneath trees hung with blue blossom.

Painted in reverse on glass.

name: Winter
description:
Michalina Janoszanka (1889–1952)

Two ravens talk on a snow-covered branch in a forest of golden trunks and falling stars.

Painted in reverse on glass.

name: The Marvellous Tree
description:
Virginia Frances Sterrett (1900–1931)

Rosalie leans towards a twisting scarlet tree hung with grapes, plums and pears, in a walled garden under a starry sky.

From Old French Fairy Tales by the Comtesse de Ségur, 1920.

name: Bonne-Biche
description:
Virginia Frances Sterrett (1900–1931)

Blondine throws her arms around the neck of the white hind Bonne-Biche, while the cat Beau-Minon sits by a coral curtain.

From Old French Fairy Tales by the Comtesse de Ségur, 1920.

name: The Tortoise
description:
Virginia Frances Sterrett (1900–1931)

Blondine rides a great patterned tortoise through a forest of pale green trunks and trailing vines.

From Old French Fairy Tales by the Comtesse de Ségur, 1920.

name: The Giant
description:
Virginia Frances Sterrett (1900–1931)

Henry, in red, shields his eyes as a green giant peers down at him over a wall of white stone and blossom.

From Old French Fairy Tales by the Comtesse de Ségur, 1920.

name: The Plant of Life
description:
Virginia Frances Sterrett (1900–1931)

Henry stands in a mountain garden thick with flowers while an old doctor in a black cloak bends over the beds with his book.

From Old French Fairy Tales by the Comtesse de Ségur, 1920.

name: The Evening Walk
description:
Virginia Frances Sterrett (1900–1931)

Rosette, in a yellow gown, walks beside the prince before a pale palace of domes and spires under a sky full of stars.

From Old French Fairy Tales by the Comtesse de Ségur, 1920.

name: Night in the Forest
description:
Virginia Frances Sterrett (1900–1931)

Violette sleeps on the moss in her wide yellow dress while Ourson keeps watch beneath trees hung with lichen and a single bright star.

From Old French Fairy Tales by the Comtesse de Ségur, 1920.

name: Still Life with Bottle, Carafe, Bread, and Wine
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A dark wine bottle, a carafe of water, a glass and a torn loaf stand on a rumpled white cloth, with a black-handled knife pointing in from the corner.

One of his earliest surviving pictures, painted in his early twenties.

C. 1862/1863, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Bazille and Camille
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A woman in a sweeping grey gown walks away beside a man in a dark suit and cap, under trees that scatter leaf shadows over her skirt.

A study for his huge picnic scene Déjeuner sur l’Herbe. The models are his friend the painter Frédéric Bazille and Camille Doncieux, later his wife.

1865, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: The Luncheon on the Grass
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Quick chalk lines set out a picnic in a forest clearing: two women in long dresses stand at the left while others sit and lie around a cloth spread on the ground.

A drawing for Déjeuner sur l’Herbe, the vast picnic painting he never finished.

C. 1865, black chalk on blue laid paper. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: The Cradle
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A wide-eyed baby lies tucked in a cradle hung with flowered blue cloth, a toy windmill beside him, while a woman in a white cap watches over him.

The baby is Jean, his first son, born in 1867.

1867, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Sainte-Adresse
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Dark fishing boats lie pulled up on a pale beach under a heavy grey sky, with a few figures at the water’s edge and cliffs curving away behind.

Sainte-Adresse is on the Normandy coast beside Le Havre, where he grew up.

1867, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Gift of Catherine Gamble Curran and Family, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art.

name: Interior, after Dinner
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A brass lamp throws a pool of yellow light on a round table where two women sit sewing, while a man leans against the mantelpiece by the fire.

1868/1869, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Argenteuil
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A sunlit path runs beside the river under a row of tall trees, with small sails on the water and the chimneys of the town on the horizon.

He lived at Argenteuil, on the Seine just outside Paris, from 1871 to 1878.

C. 1872, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: Ships Riding on the Seine at Rouen
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Two tall sailing ships ride at anchor on a rippling blue river, their pale sails and rigging mirrored in the water, with the spires of Rouen behind.

1872/1873, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: The Artist’s Garden in Argenteuil
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A great bank of red, pink and yellow dahlias fills the garden in front of a white house with blue shutters, and a couple stroll by the fence beyond.

Its full title adds: A Corner of the Garden with Dahlias.

1873, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Gift of Janice H. Levin, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art.

name: The Bridge at Argenteuil
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Sailing boats lie moored on a glittering blue river beside a stone road bridge, under a sky of piled white clouds.

1874, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Woman with a Parasol
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Seen from below on a windy hillside, a woman in white turns to look down from under a green parasol, her veil and skirts blowing, with a small boy in a straw hat behind her.

His wife Camille and their son Jean, painted outdoors, probably in a single sitting. Its full title adds: Madame Monet and Her Son.

1875, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Bridge at Argenteuil on a Gray Day
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Small boats sit on still grey water in front of a yellow boathouse, under the iron arches of a bridge and an overcast sky.

C. 1876, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: Banks of the Seine, Vétheuil
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Tall grass thick with yellow and white wildflowers fills the near bank; beyond it the blue river runs past a line of poplars under a clouded sky.

He lived in the village of Vétheuil from 1878 to 1881.

1880, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Woman Seated under the Willows
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A woman in a pale dress sits reading in long grass under slender willows, with a river and the houses of a village behind her.

The gallery suggests she may be Alice Hoschedé, later his second wife.

1880, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Jerusalem Artichoke Flowers
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A big loose bunch of yellow flowers with orange centres stands in a white vase on a round table, against a wall of pink and grey strokes.

1880, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: The Willows
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Tall, thin willows in fresh spring green rise from a meadow by the river, with the houses of the far bank showing between their trunks.

1880, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937).

name: The Artist’s Garden at Vétheuil
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A small child stands on a sunlit path between blue-and-white pots, under towering sunflowers, with steps climbing to the house behind.

1881, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: Cliffs at Pourville
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Two women rest on a green clifftop above a wide, pale blue sea scattered with tiny white sails.

Pourville is a fishing village on the Normandy coast, where he spent much of 1882.

1882, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Morning Haze
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A few trees are just visible as soft shapes in a field of white, pale blue and pink mist.

1888, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Rouen Cathedral, West Façade
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

The carved front of the cathedral fills the canvas, its doors, gable and rose window dissolved into blue and violet shadow.

One of more than thirty views of the same façade that he painted to catch it at different hours and in different weather.

1894, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Rouen Cathedral, West Façade, Sunlight
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

The carved front of the cathedral blazes cream and gold in full sun against a clear blue sky.

One of more than thirty views of the same façade that he painted to catch it at different hours and in different weather.

1894, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: The Seine at Giverny
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Rounded trees on the far bank are mirrored almost exactly in the still, pink-white water of the river at dawn.

From his Mornings on the Seine, painted from a boat near his home at Giverny.

1897, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: The Japanese Footbridge
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A blue-green wooden bridge arches over a pond covered with pink and white water lilies, closed in by reeds and willows.

The bridge and pond were in the water garden he made for himself at Giverny.

1899, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Gift of Victoria Nebeker Coberly, in memory of her son John W. Mudd, and Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg.

name: Waterloo Bridge
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

The arches of the bridge are a few smudges of blue and lilac, nearly lost in bright fog.

He painted and drew the Thames again and again from his window at the Savoy Hotel in London.

1901, pastel on blue wove paper. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Florian Carr Fund.

name: The Houses of Parliament, Sunset
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

The towers of Parliament stand as a blue silhouette against a pink and gold sky, their reflection broken up in the river below, where a single small boat passes.

1903, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Waterloo Bridge, Gray Day
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

Smoke and steam drift over the arches of the bridge, with factory chimneys behind and barges on the dull water below.

He painted and drew the Thames again and again from his window at the Savoy Hotel in London.

1903, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Waterloo Bridge, London, at Dusk
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

The bridge is barely there, a darker band across a haze of turquoise and green, with specks of light moving along it.

1904, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Waterloo Bridge, London, at Sunset
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

The arches of the bridge glow pink and apricot in a pale blue-green mist, and their colours run together in the water.

1904, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Palazzo da Mula, Venice
description:
Claude Monet (1840–1926)

A palace front with rows of pointed windows rises straight from the green-blue canal, where two gondolas wait at a doorway.

Painted on his only visit to Venice, in the autumn of 1908.

1908, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Eddy Cassatt
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A fair-haired boy in a red velvet suit with a lace collar stands holding a riding crop, a grey terrier sitting at his side.

Her nephew Edward, about six years old. She signed it in the corner: Eddy from Aunt Mary. Its full title adds: Edward Buchanan Cassatt.

1875, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Gift from the Family of Col. Edward Buchanan Cassatt.

name: Woman with a Fan
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A woman in a pale green dress and a white scarf tied under her chin looks away to one side, an open golden fan resting in her lap.

C. 1878/1879, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: The Loge
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

Two young women in white evening gowns sit close together in a box at the theatre, both looking out towards the stage.

C. 1878-1880, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Little Girl in a Blue Armchair
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A little girl in a white dress sprawls in a bright blue armchair, one arm behind her head, while a small brown dog sleeps in the chair beside hers.

Her friend Edgar Degas advised her on this picture and worked on part of the background himself.

1878, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Young Girl at a Window
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A young woman in a white dress and bonnet sits in front of a balcony railing in bright sun, a small dog on her lap.

C. 1883-1884, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund, 1909).

name: Children Playing on the Beach
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

Two small girls in blue dresses and pale pinafores sit back to back on the sand, one busy with a pail and a wooden shovel.

1884, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: Girl Arranging Her Hair
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A girl in a loose pale blue chemise sits on a ladderback chair, head tipped back, holding the end of her long brown braid.

Degas admired this picture and kept it for the rest of his life.

1886, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Child in a Straw Hat
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A young girl in a grey dress and a wide straw hat stands with her hands clasped, head tipped to one side and a doubtful look on her face.

C. 1886, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Portrait of a Lady
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A smiling grey-haired woman in a black coat and a black hat trimmed with pink flowers leans one elbow on the back of a flowered chair.

C. 1887, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Woman with a Red Zinnia
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A red-haired young woman in a white dress leans on the back of a green garden bench, head resting on her hand, looking down at a red flower she holds.

Its full title adds: Revery.

1891-1892, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: The Boating Party
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

Seen from behind, a man in dark blue rows a green and white boat; facing him sit a woman in a blue dress and the baby in pink sprawled across her lap.

Painted at Antibes on the Mediterranean coast of France.

1893/1894, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Woman with a Sunflower
description:
Mary Cassatt (1844–1926)

A woman in golden yellow sits in a green chair with a child on her lap, the two of them looking together into a small hand mirror.

C. 1905, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: The Sisters
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

Two dark-haired women in matching white dresses with blue dots sit side by side on a sofa, black ribbons at their necks.

1869, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Gift of Mrs. Charles S. Carstairs.

name: The Mother and Sister of the Artist
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

An older woman in black sits reading a book, while a younger woman in white watches from the sofa behind her.

Her mother and her sister Edma. Edouard Manet repainted parts of the mother before it went to the Salon, which upset Morisot.

1869/1870, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: The Artist's Sister at a Window
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

A young woman in a long white dress sits in an armchair by an open window, looking down at the fan in her lap.

Her sister Edma.

1869, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: The Harbor at Lorient
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

A young woman in white sits on a low stone wall under a pink parasol, looking down at the wide blue harbour; boats and a town line the far shore.

The woman is her sister Edma. Morisot gave the picture to Edouard Manet.

1869, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: Peonies
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

A pink peony bows over the rim of a clear glass, with a bud and two other flowers beside it and one fallen petal on the table.

C. 1869, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Hanging the Laundry out to Dry
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

White sheets hang on lines across a grassy yard where women are at work, with a house and a distant town behind, all in quick, thick strokes.

1875, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.

name: Young Woman with a Straw Hat
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

A woman in a pale blue dress is seen in profile, her straw hat tied under her chin with a wide purple ribbon.

1884, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: In the Dining Room
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

A young woman in a dark blue dress and a white apron stands in a dining room, looking straight out, her hands held up at her chest.

1886, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Girl in a Boat with Geese
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

Four white geese line the near bank of a lake while a rowing boat drifts on the water behind them, among greens and blues.

C. 1889, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection.

name: The Artist's Daughter with a Parakeet
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

A young girl in a coral dress sits with her hands in her lap, looking straight out at us.

Her daughter Julie Manet, aged about eleven.

1890, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Chester Dale Collection.

name: Young Girl with an Apron
description:
Berthe Morisot (1841–1895)

A girl with a blue ribbon in her red-brown hair sits with her hands in the pockets of her white apron; behind her a small table holds a vase of flowers.

1891, oil on canvas. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon.
